planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring after the last frost directly into loose, well-drained dune or beach sand in full sun; seed germination is slow and erratic, so nursery-propagated softwood cuttings are the more reliable route to establishment.

directions: Bay Lavender is a sprawling, mound-forming succulent subshrub of primary and secondary coastal dunes, prized for the dense whorls of felted, silvery-gray leaves clustered at its branch tips that reflect intense sun and salt spray. Small white, fragrant flowers open in coiled scorpioid cymes typical of the borage family, followed by pale drupe-like fruits that are dispersed by shorebirds and ocean currents. It thrives in pure sand with no supplemental fertility, tolerates direct salt spray and occasional storm overwash, and helps anchor dune faces alongside sea oats and beach morning glory. Because it is frost-tender and best suited to the mildest, southernmost stretches of the Gulf Coast, gardeners farther inland or north should treat it as a container or greenhouse-protected specimen rather than a reliable landscape perennial.
